utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Once again it was necessary for us to start late for the staff to be able to complete their work following this morning's proceedings. Mr. Nicholls, are we ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We're ready, Your Honour, if we could bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karpuzi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We continue now with your evidence. Yes, Mr. Nicholls. Could I remind you that the affirmation you made at the beginning still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nicholls: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karpuzi.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we left off yesterday, you'd been telling us how in mid-June and into July you had split your duties; part of the time you were keeping records, and you told us about that duty, and the other time you spent you said as a guard duty observing the terrain. And I want to ask you a few questions now about that aspect of your duty in July 1998 observing the terrain. Okay?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember in July 1998 if the position you were assigned to to observe the terrain, if it had a special -- a specific name or number?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was point 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talked about this a little bit on your first day of testimony when you talked about observing the Komorane Serb checkpoint, but could you describe what your duties were when you were at position 1 in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duty was to observe the terrain, to see the movements of the enemy, to check how many forces were heading towards Komorane and Cuka, how can of them came, how many of them left -- I mean the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as part of this was traffic on the Pristina-Peja road monitored?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this observation from point 1, how many hours during a 24-hour day would somebody with observing from position 1 during July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe four, six hours depending on the soldiers -- on the number of soldiers. If we were two in a shift, it might be four or six. I don't remember accurately how many hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many shifts were there in a day?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had non-stop shifts. We kept surveillance for 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During this surveillance would any notes be taken of what you observed?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think yes, but I cannot tell you for sure. To my recollection we used to keep notes about the number of the enemy forces that came and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember the names -- I should say pseudonyms of any of the soldiers who served with you at position 1 during July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember some of them like Uka, Graniti, Motori. I don't remember more than these because a long time has passed since that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. I'd like to now show you a book. This is U002-3460 through U002-3492. I have a copy here which I've tabbed for the witness. You can open that up, Witness, maybe to the first tab which is an entry for 2nd of July, which would be page 4 of the English text. First of all, do you remember whether I showed you this book on Sunday when we met?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember -- take a look at that 2nd of July entry. Does your pseudonym appear anywhere on the page, Shala? That should be the first page with a red tab on it to help you find it. It's -- it has the number 3465 on the end -- on the page on your version.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who does it say were the other soldiers who were on shift you on that date?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it's written Shala, Motori, Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember whether Hoxha ever was on duty with you at position 1?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you just look at the entries from that shift which you were on, I'm not going to ask you if you specifically remember the entries that are written down there, if you specifically remember, for instance, the white Land Rover that is referred to, but do these appear to be the types of entries that are noted down?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you now to look at the entry for the 22nd of July. That's on page 37 of our English version, and it should be the last red tab in your version, sir. It will be the last page with a red sticker on it, sir, if I've marked it correctly. Do you see your pseudonym, Shala, on that page?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which other soldiers were serving with you on that day, on 22nd of July, does it say?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written Gazi also here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, if you look at the entries on that page, are those the types of entries which you would have made when you were on duty observing the terrain?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, does that book appear to you to be an accurate photocopy of the notebook from position 1 when you served there in July? Can you tell?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I have for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd ask to admit that, Your Honour, and give it a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Prosecution Exhibit P129.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it should be the English and Albanian versions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P129 will be the Albanian version and P129A will be the English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm done with that, Mr. Karpuzi, thank you. Sir, please look at this image. This is image 8 from Exhibit P1. If we could put that on the ELMO. I believe we looked at this photo yesterday and we also looked at it on Sunday when I met you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we can give the witness a pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first of all before you mark that, on the 26th of July during the battle were you at position 1 or were you at a different position during the fighting on the 26th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at position 2. When some soldiers went to Rahovec to take care of the population, we, some soldiers, had to move from position number 1 to position number 2 in the absence of these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when -- as close as you can remember when was the date when you were moved from position 1 to position 2?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember accurately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember approximately how long you had been at position 2 before the fighting started?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe three or four days, even five maybe. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at the image to your left - familiarise yourself with that for a moment - could you try to find the point of position 2 where you were on duty during the fighting on the battle of 26th July 1998. Take your time if you need to.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you can mark it, why don't you write a 2 where you think -- where you remember you were at position 2 on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the 26th? Because on the 25th I was at another position. It was also called number 2, but when I was injured on that day I was on a higher position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't you mark first where you were on the 26th of July at a position when you were injured. Mark that with a number "2."

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the witness has made a mark at a road near where three roads meet. I think it's hard to read as a 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe we can give you a better pen or could you make a bigger 2 there, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you also mark position 1, which is where you were, talking about the bulk of July, when you were on duty observing the terrain.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may not be very accurate because I can't see it very well, but it is approximately there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you mark that with a little bit larger number 1, please. I can't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Marking is fine while the ink is wet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's give you a different pen and see if that works better. Sorry, sir. Try to use that pen to mark position 1.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it works, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And make it large. You can use more ink.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that you can see now the red marking on top of the white one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that's probably sufficient. And could you draw an arrow to position 1, just draw an arrow right to where you've marked position 1.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean to draw a circle there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. If you could, just draw a line with an arrow pointing to position 1 to make it a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's good. Thank you. And now could you try to point out the other position which you said you were at immediately before you moved to the position you've indicated with a 2, where you were on the 26th of July, 1998, during the fighting. Where is that third position?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about the 25th because I already marked the position on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. If you could mark the position you were at on the 25th. Mark that with a 3, a large 3, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you can refer to that diagram if you need to, but could you please briefly describe to me the battle of the 26th July 1998 as it appeared to you from your perspective at position 2.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Sunday the forces were at a great distance. There were over 400 vehicles. In the evening of Friday when we saw them coming from Pristina road, all the soldiers took up positions. And we counted them entering in the direction of Drenoc and Komorane from Cuka. There were over 400 vehicles. It was night, Friday night, when we saw them. It was about midnight. Yes, it was Friday. On Saturday, on the 25th, they started shelling early morning, but from a distance. They used all possible means at their disposal -- at the disposal of the Yugoslav army. They used them -- all ammunitions against us. It was sometime in the evening of 25th that we saw some green shells being fired -- blue, sorry. After four or five minutes we felt drowsy and sleepy; it was because of some poison and we -- our tears -- our eyes started to shed tears. It was the poison that made us feel that bad. When the shells fell near us, we felt like we were in a coma and we asked each other whether we were alive. In the evening we withdrew from that position because the Serb forces came very near, maybe 50, 60 metres away from us. The tanks were positioned there. And tanks started to fire at us. They played music. They were celebrating. We didn't have heavy vehicles to fight back at them, heavy armaments. So on the 26th we were on this high ground position and we waited until the tanks set out in the direction of the position where I was located. They fired at us as hard as they could. While they stopped for a while firing to see whether anyone was still alive, I attempted to fire a mortar at them; it was about 120, 30 metres from the position I was in. The first three shells did -- were not activated. The fourth one I think was activated when the tank was close. The fourth one, as I said, this one I managed to fire at the tank and I managed -- I hit it. But when -- because of the explosion, there were two barrels of oil -- with oil which also exploded. There were some soldiers, policemen, paramilitaries, they were not dressed in green uniform, but with dark blue uniforms. And I saw two bodies flying up in the air because of the explosion. The second tank which was next to the first one coming -- of course the tank saw the explosion and it fired at us, it shelled us. And we all were -- flew up in the air. When we fell on the ground -- as I said yesterday, I had had an injury. So when I fell back on the ground, I had -- again I broke my hip. And I told my comrades to withdraw. Isak Demiri was one of the comrades. He pulled me and we started to walk about -- to withdraw in the direction of the hill. We went behind the hill. I remember what happened until that moment; then I no longer remembered what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive any medical treatment for these injuries? Did you get any help?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe where you were treated.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw myself in Klecke in an ambulance, a makeshift ambulance. I didn't know where I was, but I know that the other patients who were there told me we were in Klecka and we were being treated. I stayed there for two weeks I think. For 11 days I kept count, but my comrades told me that for two or three days I had lost consciousness, so I didn't remember how long exactly I stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Isak Musliu in Lapusnik on the 26th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th I remember having seen him. On the 26th it was impossible to see anything because of the shelling, because we were staying in that position, whereas Isak Musliu was positioned in another place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your first day of testimony you talked about how Isak Musliu was present all the time in Lapusnik until the gorge fell, and that's on page 34 of the LiveNote for that day. But you also said that at some point he went to Rahovec to help in those villages. When did he go to Rahovec and when did he return, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know for sure whether it was during the time we passed from position number 1 to rainforest position number 2. I know that these soldiers were helping the population to leave Rahovec. So I do not remember accurately whether it was the 16th, 17th, or 18th. I don't want to lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you don't remember, that's fine. When you were evacuated or taken somehow to Klecka on the 26th of July after you'd been injured in the fighting, what happened to the records you had been keeping in Gzim Gashi's compound, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know what happened with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anybody was able to retrieve those, before the Serbs re-took the area I mean?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm almost done, Witness. If you can tell us now what you did very briefly after you left the makeshift hospital in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After all the soldiers started to go back to their own villages, everybody thought best to go to his own village because they knew the terrain better. I did the same, so I went back to my village; and my family thought I was dead. Of course I -- we rejoiced, me and them, when we saw each other. Some comrades, I didn't know that they were members of the KLA; some comrades from my village came and asked me, Now that you are back, what can we do? Where to go? And I told them, There is nowhere you can go. Your duty is to go to the population and defend them against Serb police and army. So they asked me to lead them even though I was in difficult -- in a bad situation, I mean physically. I agreed to lead them for a month I think. And then after that period I asked them to release me of that duty because I didn't feel well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm reminded, Your Honour, if I could ask for an exhibit number for the image 8 which the witness has marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit 130.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you five photographs now, Witness, the front and back of the photographs and ask you just a few questions about those.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can put these on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first is U007-2255 and 2256, that's the front and back of the photograph. Now, do you recognise that photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's written on the back of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "November 1998, Ruzhdi V. Karpuzi (Shala)."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that photograph taken of you in November of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My brother took the picture -- not only this, also some others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who made the writing? Who typed your name and the date on the back, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother, but this happened after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to admit those please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "those"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, it's two separate ERN numbers because it's the front and the back of the photograph, but we don't have the actual photograph in evidence, we have a copy. So it's -- it can be assigned one exhibit number but it's two separate sheets of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P131.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could have the next photos, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, do you recall this photo, sir?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, this is a photo taken of you in November of 1998, with the same description on the back as the previous one. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could ask that this be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P132.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, we can do that one. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at this photo, sir. Do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who are the three men in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's me, Haxhi Shala, and Rexhep Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just read what is typed on the back of the card.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ruzhdi Karpuzi, Shal; Haxhi Shala; Rexhep Bajrami Leletiq".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the date on the photo?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: December 1998, "Ne Shale." And then the names "Ruzhdi Karpuzi (Shala)", "Haxhi Shala (Topi)", and "Rexhep Bajrami (Kushtrimi)."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the previous photographs we looked at you were not in a camouflage uniform. In this photo you have a camouflage uniform. If you remember, when did you get that camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photo was taken after I received the uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. I just wonder if you remember when it was that you received your uniform.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I can't remember accurately. I know it was new, but I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd ask to admit this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P133.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's me. On 15th of November, when the trial started, all -- everybody was looking at me with some disbelief because of some news broadcast by -- from here alleging that I have said Haradin Bala wore black uniform, he was responsible for the prison camp, and all -- such things. I immediately informed the Tribunal office in Pristina and here about this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know when this photograph was taken, if you look at the date on the back? Is that an accurate date that's printed there?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is not accurate. The date is not accurate. I can guarantee that the date marked here is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was taken in June, either May or June. I can't be certain. It was taken at my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll show you one more photo, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'd ask that that be exhibited as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecution Exhibit P134.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you explain to the Trial Chamber what's depicted in this photograph, who these people are and what's going on in this photo.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken near the monument of Ymer Alushani in Lapusnik on the occasion of the anniversary of his death. Everybody could take a picture at that time, not only us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what year this photograph was taken, on which anniversary?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during the anniversary of Ymer Alushani, aka Voglushi. When this, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm looking at the back. Can you just read what the top two lines are, what's written on the back of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first line there is a question mark, meaning that I didn't remember the name of the person. Number 2, again, I did not remember the name because a long time passed. Only Ismajli and Bokseri Fushtic; Ruzhdi Karpuzi, Shale; Muhamet, I knew the guy as Muhamet, but not the last name. Lulzim Thaqi (Luli) Komoran; Fatmir Gashi (Fati) Lapusnik; Enver Mulaku (Bacaloku) Komoran; Ramadan Zogu (Shaban Polluzha); Agim Zogaj (Motori); number 10, question mark; number 11, question mark. Number 12, I knew only Sopi from Lapusnik; Bajram Bujupi (Bajra) Komoran; Halil Kolushi (Kuburja), Baice [sic]; Kolshi (Homeini), Baice [sic]; Rrahman Nishori (Xhaxhi), Komorane; Ismet Hoxha (Baci), Nekovc [sic]; Haradin Bala (Shala), Korrotice; Gzim Sopi, Lapusnik; Arsim Gashi, Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the very top two lines, before the numbers start, what is written there in your language?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the beginning, at the top line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think it says --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says near memorial of Voglushi, Ymer Alushani, in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who typed up the words and names on the back of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother so that I could have them as a keepsake at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you tell him who the people were and he typed it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could give this exhibit a number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P135.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Karpuzi, I don't have any further questions for you at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask now to move into evidence Mr. Karpuzi's two statements which we've been using over the last two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And your basis for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, they've been used extensively in my direct examination; they've been used to try to refresh the witness's memory. The Chamber has had them before them, so I think they should be part of the record and I think that whatever weight the Chamber may decide to give them could be determined later after more evidence has been submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it's any assistance, and without setting a precedent, there's no objection for these documents to be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Is there any other view from the Defence counsel? Well, then, firstly the -- We seem to have dealt with three statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Two I believe, Your Honour, unless I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're only dealing with the statement in July of 2003?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. And the one from just this last Sunday, the 6th of February, 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Firstly, the July 2003 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P136.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And perhaps -- I think we should have both languages, the original English and the Albanian translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original of that statement, P136, in Albanian; and the English translation will be Prosecution Exhibit P136A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then the statement of the 6th of February, 2005.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement of the 6th February, 2005, the Albanian-language statement will be Prosecution Exhibit P137; and the English translation, P137A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm invited to go first. Cross-examined by Mr. Topolski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karpuzi, I represent Mr. Isak Musliu. If you look to your left, you'll see it's me who's talking. I want to try and deal with your evidence in the order in which events happened as best I can. If I've understood what you told us a couple of days ago correctly, you decided to join the KLA some time after the death of Adem Jashari which I suggest took place in February of 1998, and you finally joined the KLA on the 18th of April that year. Have I understood your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I just want to deal first of all, if I may please, with your joining. You joined in Likovc and you tried to join more than once before finally joining on the 18th of April. Again, have I correctly understood your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasions that you tried to join unsuccessfully before the 18th of April, one of the problems was, as you put it, they regretted that they had no weapon to give you and you had to go and find your own. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had several attempts to find a weapon, and eventually a hunting weapon was given to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But with no ammunition. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not given any ammunition, bullets to fire, with the hunting rifle; that's what you hold us a couple of days ago. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not listening -- I can't listen to the Albanian version. In the middle of the statement, then there is a break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid my skills or powers of influence don't extend that far. I can't help you. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you try again with your question, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question, Mr. Karpuzi, is this: You were given a rifle but no ammunition. Is that right? Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you. They gave me several bullets. Approximately -- I can't tell you the exact number, but there were just a few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were given no uniform. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've just been shown a number of different photographs taken much later when you are wearing two different kinds of uniform, I suggest, a camouflage uniform and what appears to be a black uniform. First of all, would you agree with that? And if you don't, I'll show you the photographs again.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you explain one thing here, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning I didn't have a uniform. It was a civilian gear, different civilian clothing. Some had jeans, some, let's say, had black jeans and a black jacket; but mainly they were civilian clothing. While in December, I don't know exactly when, I know there was snow, I was given a uniform; it was in the end of 1998, sometime around December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'd been able to take a picture of you at the moment you received your injury in the battle of Lapusnik on the 25th of July, would we have seen you in a uniform of any kind?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What took you to Lapusnik, as I understand your evidence, on the 8th of May was that you heard detonations, explosions, from there where you were in your village of Shale. Again, have I understood your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I be right in suggesting to you, Mr. Karpuzi, that the village of Shale is something like 9 kilometres from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately. And what kind of explosions could you hear in Shale occurring in what you thought must be Lapusnik on the 8th of May? What kind of explosions were you hearing?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Explosions could be heard and I knew that combat was going on somewhere. I thought it was in Komorane because it was coming from that direction, and after I went there I understood correctly that that's where it was -- the fight was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe my question wasn't clear enough. Were you hearing shelling by artillery? Were you hearing grenades? Were you hearing machine-gun fire? What kind of detonations were you hearing 9 kilometres away in Shale on the 8th of May?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of detonations they were, but mainly there were explosions, detonations. Not machine-gun fire. It was just explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You travelled to Lapusnik partly by tractor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to Kishna Reka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from Kishna Reka on foot?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there you met others who had got to Lapusnik ahead of you in order to fight. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe 12 or 13, or am I wrong about the number?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The group that I met, so we were approximately five or six with -- including me or without me, I'm not quite sure here -- but it was five or six persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to take you through an exercise that Mr. Nicholls took you through more than once, and I'm going to try and do it differently in the hope that it might clear up exactly where various firing positions were. Do you understand? And what I'm going to do is I'm going to give you a clean version of image 8. It's not quite clean because I've marked it with some numbers and some letters and I've put some blank stickers on it in the hope that this might make things clearer. I hold it up so the Tribunal and my friends can see it across the room. Absent from any objection, I hope that we can do it like this and put it on the ELMO and go through it together. Sorry about the speech, Mr. Karpuzi, I'm just explaining what I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't have any objection, but could I just see it? I can't see it across the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Of course. Could you just show it to Mr. Nicholls first, please. Thank you to Mr. Guy-Smith who's allowed me to take this sheet out of his folder. Your Honours, obviously it's the witness's evidence. Those stickers can be moved and that's why they're there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karpuzi, have a look, please, will you, at this. Now, the first thing I want to draw your attention to is that I've endeavoured to identify each of these squares. So what I've done is I've put numbers along the top. Do you see? 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here at the top, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if we could pull back a bit so the whole -- as much of this as possible can be seen for the moment, please. Too big, can't do it. All right. At least I think that's what was being said to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you move it down so we can see the top of the -- we can see a number of unidentified numbers in brackets. Are they the ones to which you refer?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm referring to, yes. If your seen is anything as bad as mine it's almost impossible to see. May I indicate I have written above each square of different sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, 6 columns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Down the left side, if it can be moved slightly across, so we see the left-hand side, I have written -- again, against each line of squares I've written A, B, C, and D. Sorry to do this like an infant school, but it's the only way I can understand this. Therefore, Mr. Karpuzi, what we should be able to do is if we looking at any particular square, I should be able to give you a number and a letter and you should be able to go to it. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To help the record, by squares do you mean the grid reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, grid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand me, Mr. Karpuzi?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. It's not clear. If I said to you: Put your finger on grid number 1A, would you do that for me, please? 1A, go to grid 1A and put your finger on it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. We do understand each other. Right. There's a red line on that plan -- image. Do you see it? Yes, exactly that. It starts in 2A and goes all the way down to 5D. Do you follow it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me tell you what that is because I don't think anyone's told you that yet. That is said to be a line representing KLA fighting positions in Lapusnik. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. You and I are going to work together along that line and along those tabs that I've put there. It's your evidence, not mine; therefore, if you want to move a tab you must do so. Do you understand me? Do you understand what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought you said that this were my notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. This is my handiwork, but you're going to finish it off by giving the evidence about it, Mr. Karpuzi. All right? Let's just start and we'll see how we get on. Look at square number 2A.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's it. Just where you've put your finger I suggest there was a fighting position called Guri, G-u-r-i, meaning rock. That is the rock overlooking the Peja-Pristina road which you see running across the plan. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly there, there it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly there. Well, then would you be good enough to write on that red tab "G," for Guri. With a pen. It should be clear. Mr. Guy-Smith's stickers work.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Come along the red line with me to square 3A, please, and you should come to the next tab.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. I suggest, Mr. Karpuzi, that that red tab shows as close as, I suggest, we can get to it the position of point number 1. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. Would you be good enough to write the figure "1" on the red tab that we've just been talking about.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Down the line to the text tab, we're now in square 3B. Mr. Karpuzi, I suggest that, again, indicates approximately the position of point 2. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. Would you write "2" there, please, on that tab.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming down the line to the next tab, now square 4B, again as best I can I suggest that is the position of fighting point number 3. Do you agree with me about that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. Would you write "3" then on that tab, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming down the plan - and we're now at grid 4C and we're now in a slightly different position where I've put a tab - I suggest that is the approximate or as close to the position of point number 4, fighting position number 4 at Lapusnik. Do you agree with that? Don't write anything unless you agree. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From above I cannot understand it very well, but this should be approximately how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, of course we all understand the difficulties. Now, there's one more red tab there, and what I'm going to suggest was - and it's slightly off the plan deliberately - this was where soldiers were held in reserve to join whichever point they needed to join during the course of the various fighting at Lapusnik. Again, slightly off the plan, so a little difficult. But do you agree with me that there was a group of reserve soldiers kept around there where that last tab is, at grid 4D? Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there were, but I don't know about it. But there were civilians who would come to report and then go back because of the weapons, because there was lack of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And I'm suggesting that they may have been kept or, rather, stayed at that area. But if you can't be sure, we can move on. You can't be sure; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you anything in that. Now, looking back at the plan, please, if we could just have it more centrally positioned for a moment. Again, I don't think this was explained to you but I want to tell you what you're looking at. Would you go to grid 3C where you will see an area circled in red. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That, Mr. Karpuzi, shows the place you know as Gzim's compound and another compound across the road, and I'm going to show you photographs of the place in a minute. But do you agree with me - I know it's difficult looking at the aerial photograph - but that is where Gzim's compound was, in that red circle?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be seen clearly, and once I cannot see it clearly I cannot say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's a perfectly reasonable answer, if I may say so, but you can take it from me that that's where Gzim's compound is. All right? Will you accept my word for it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will accept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. Now, I just want you to look carefully at Gzim's compound and that circle for a moment that goes round it. And I want you to put your finger or the pointer on the circle at approximately where the 4 would be on a watch, 4.00. All right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. All right. Now, I want you to come gently across the grid to the right towards the border, if you like, of that grid until I tell you to stop. Would you do that for me, please. Point to the red circle approximately where 4 would be on a clock and then move it downwards and to the right until I say stop. Would you move it downwards towards the 4, towards unit 4, until I tell you to stop. No, you're going in the wrong direction, Mr. Karpuzi, the other way. Go towards the red tab 4. Keep going. Yes, that line. Draw that line, but come down the plan towards the number 4 with the pointer. A bit more --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have no objection if Mr. Topolski --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop there, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Nicholls, I just wanted the witness to stop. My friend I think has something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. I was going to say I have no objection to you drawing his attention directly to the spot you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. I should have put another tab there, maybe I will during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've got there, so keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I just want to get him into a place there and then I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you stopped - and I know it's difficult, Mr. Karpuzi - was one of the houses where Mr. Qerqizi was based. It's a little group of houses there. I'm going to put a sticker on during the break. Did you ever go to Qerqizi's base in Lapusnik, the house he stayed in?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doing the best you can, looking at that plan, now I've told you where Gzim's compound is, do you agree with me that that could be - and that's the highest you could put it I expect - that could be where Qerqizi stayed for some of the time in Lapusnik? Do you agree? That's it, just about there?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: With a slight sigh of relief, I wonder if we might have a break, as Your Honour has indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It hasn't been that much of a strain, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I have your leave to put another tab on the plan. It's now in the witness's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I was just going to say we should mark the last spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can keep your eye on what happens. And if there is no further issue raised when we return, we'll take it that the spot has been successfully marked. We will resume at 5 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm very grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karpuzi, I want to go back to this image, and I want to go back, please -- if we could have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karpuzi, I made a mistake and I'm going to suggest to you, sir, that you agreed with my mistake. So I'm going to see if I can put my mistake right and see whether you're prepared to agree with me. And the mistake I made was in the precise position of the rock, Guri. Now, I've of course alerted Mr. Nicholls and Mr. Whiting to this and precisely what I'm going to do. What I want to do is look again at the position of where Guri the rock was and indeed is. I'm going to suggest, Mr. Karpuzi, that you do this, please: I want you to look at the junction between grid 2 and 3 first of all, that vertical line at the top of the plan. The line -- that's right. Just put your pen on there. That's it. Exactly that. I want you to come down that line to where your pen is, which is the junction of A and B. Just about there, I suggest, we see what appears to be a clearing of trees. That is where Guri, the rock, is. I put it too close to the road first time around. There. Now, look carefully. I know it's difficult, it's an aerial view. You must not agree with me, just -- listen to me a minute. You must not agree with me simply because I say so; it's your evidence, not mine. So look carefully at where I've suggested in fact Guri position was. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Have I made that clear enough for Your Honours as to where we are? I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what do you say?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said even earlier that I can't see very well and I've never had any opportunity to see an aerial view, so I see a difference between this image and what I might know. So I'm not very accurate in showing -- pinpointing at the right, exact place of the rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, in that case the only, I suggest, Your Honours, fair way of proceeding is the witness put a question mark against the letter G on the tab that he's marked because it is not his evidence that he can be clear about it. Unless my friend objects. I'm grateful. So Mr. Karpuzi, against the letter G you've written on the tab there, can you put a question mark.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Now --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see things very clearly. I cannot really distinguish the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We absolutely understand. Now, I've put two -- again, with Mr. Nicholls' knowledge and kind approval, I've put two new stickers on there during the break and I want you to help me if you can. Go to square 3B, please. There's an empty, blank sticker there at the moment. Now --

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to suggest this to you, Mr. Karpuzi: that Qerqizi occupied two different houses in Lapusnik at different times and you might well have visited them both. So my first question is: Is that the position as you remember it? Two different houses and you may well have visited him in both at different times.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used to move from one house to the other. So we didn't stay long in one place. We used to visit one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand. And of course evidence about this can be given much later on in the case if need be, but I want to see if you can help. So I'm going to make a suggestion. That blank tab that I've located in 3B is pointing towards, if you look carefully, what seem to be a group of houses. I suggest that in that little group there is a house of a man called Avni Gashi, and it was in Avni Gashi's house that Qerqizi was based in the early days in Lapusnik in May of 1998, and I further suggest, sir, that you may well have visited him in that part of the village. Can you help with me those suggestions?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming down the plan we were looking before the break at a place I was inviting -- again suggesting to you that this was another base, another house occupied by Qerqizi. We're now in square 3C, and I've, again with Mr. Nicholls' kind approval, put a blank sticker pointing towards where I suggest another house is. And I'm going to help you with a name again of a villager, Mr. Karpuzi, Ferat Sopi, S-o-p-i. His house occupied by Qerqizi in June and July of 1998 where you might well have visited. Do you agree that is possible?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not Ferhat but Ferat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. My question, however, was: Did you visit Qerqizi in a house in that part of the village?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to go back finally to a tab at the very bottom of the image. Could we raise the image slightly on the screen, please, Usher. Thank you. It's blank at the moment. Again, it's my fault, so I'm sorry I was explaining this wrongly before the break. Mr. Karpuzi, what I'm attempting to show here is a point just off the plan -- just off the photograph which was usually kept empty but was a point to which soldiers could go if the point they were occupying near it was getting shelled or attacked in some way. Now, do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear. At the beginning I didn't have -- I didn't receive translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This place I have shown at the bottom of the image just off the photograph, in that part of the village was another point but it did not usually have soldiers in it. It was a place where you could run to if the point you were occupying was, for example, being shelled or attacked in some other way. Now, do you remember a place down there in the village to the south of this photograph that was like that in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many houses there. I don't understand what do you mean exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to dwell on it. I would like you, please, just to mark the two Qerqizi houses we were looking at, otherwise in months to come when we come back to this perhaps we're not going to see what you say about them. Could you go back to the red tab in 3B, the empty one.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And could you put "Q" there, the letter Q.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you do the same for the other tab where you've identified Qerqizi's house may have been, down in square 3C, the one that's empty at the moment. Could you again put a "Q" there, please. That's it.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a Q? It looks like a G to me. It's a Q?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a Q.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a Q there, please. Is that what you've done?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you can say also soft Q.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I just want to ask you one or two questions about the scene generally here, please, these various points, these various firing positions. I want to suggest this to you: At each point, around each point we've marked here, there were in Lapusnik two or three bunkers. Do you understand what I mean by a bunker? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the points roughly marked here were trenches dug by soldiers and villagers as another line of defence. Do you agree with me about that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure to everyone's relief, I'm going to leave that. I hope that it may in due course it will be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I ask that that separate plan, image, be admitted, Your Honours. Just to guard those stickers, I hope we may put some Sellotape over it so that those stickers that are likely to be lost in the course of days and weeks. I hope that may be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure that can be arranged practically.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, could I ask for a number for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be DM3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: DM3. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Karpuzi, you can forget that now and we can move on to other things. I want to ask you a couple of questions about Ymer Alushani who died on the 26th of July. When is it you say that Ymer Alushani, Voglushi, was elected as one of the leaders at Lapusnik? When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an exact date, but it was after the first fighting in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, if it wasn't yesterday it was the day before, that Voglushi proposed Qerqiz to become one of the leaders after the 18th of May. Now, is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it follows, doesn't it, that if Voglushi had proposed Qerqiz after the 18th of May, Voglushi must have been elected before the 18th of May? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it was. First it was Voglushi who was elected, then it was he who proposed that Qerqizi be elected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to be clear about this. The position regarding the election of Voglushi, as I've understood your evidence, was that it was literally that; he was asked if he would like to be, be prepared to be, a leader. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a contest? Was there a leadership election? Did anyone stand against him? And was there a vote on it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We asked him, Ymer, to assume some responsibility, to become a leader for us. Because everybody -- he was known by the soldiers and by the local population because he was from Komorane very near Lapusnik, and he was greatly respected. That's why we asked him that he take over this responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to be clear about Qerqizi and his position. We know, because you've told us and I don't dispute it, that Voglushi proposed Qerqizi to the fighters there to become one of the leaders. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Qerqizi was not, I repeat, not being elected to become the one and only commander in Lapusnik, was he? I suggest Qerqizi was elected to become the leader of one of the units in Lapusnik. Am I right or am I wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am right. Good. Having dealt with that, I want to move on to Qerqizi in Lapusnik, and more specifically Qerqizi out of Lapusnik. I want to understand what you're saying. At various points yesterday you were telling us, Mr. Nicholls, that Qerqizi was in Lapusnik all the time. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said so. When -- except for the fighting when he was asked to go to render assistance to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I suggest the position is that there was a period in late -- mid- to late July. I've been specific with another witness; I'll be specific with you. The 18th to the 24th of July, six/seven days, when Qerqizi was not in Lapusnik. Now, I don't think for one moment you were keeping a diary, Mr. Karpuzi; you were fighting a war. So I hope my sensible question is: Could I be right? Is there a week or so when Qerqizi was not to be seen in Lapusnik, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I answered yesterday this question and even today. It is true during this period I remember he was in Rahovec, and you know why? Because I remember very well when they left for Rahovec there was an old soldier and he started to cry that his friends, his comrades, didn't take him along with them in Rahovec to fight there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Qerqizi of course by this time was one of the leaders, so it would have been noticed, wouldn't it, that he was not there because someone would have had to have led the unit while he was away. That was the position, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I suppose one of the reasons you might not know because it rather depends what unit you were in. Were you in the unit led by Qerqizi or were you in someone else's unit?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at position number 1 in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your leader in July?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your leader, who was in charge, if anybody, of your unit, number 1, in mid- to late July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: His last name was Zogi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mjeshtri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you one or two questions about documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: And for this purpose, please, Your Honours could we go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to show you now not a plan of the village but shots of houses, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I wonder, could the witness please be given P6, the locations booklet. And also could he be given -- could I ask Mr. Nicholls help what exhibit number that was given or Mr. Younis? 128, thank you. Could he also have 128, please. Your Honours, it's the single photograph of the compound. Can we just give him this one first, the single one first, P128.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask you to look at that, Mr. Karpuzi, would you bear with me and forgive me. I just want to ask you a couple of more questions about documentation before we move on to that, so forgive me. You say you kept records of the details of soldiers who had come to fight in Lapusnik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were to tell investigators when they came to sit down with you and take statements about this case that you did that at the request of Qerqizi. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that Qerqiz requested me to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who requested you to do that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To take notes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, details of the soldiers, names, places they came from, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this, Ymer proposed to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in suggesting to you that from time to time you would take those records or some of them to where Qerqizi was staying, in one of the houses?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm wrong about that. You kept them then, these records, in Gzim's oda. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go anywhere else as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no place for them to go, these documents, because all they contained was details about soldiers, their weapons, their marital status, something that was not secret. They were placed on a shelf in the oda, these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I give the Court an idea of what we're talking about. Are these loose sheets of paper? Are they in a book, a file, what?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For every soldier, there existed a piece of paper with their name, last name, date of birth, father's name, the village that person came from. And the other piece of paper contained data about the economic status of the family. And about the weapon, the number of the weapon that the person has signed for, whether it was automatic, rifle 10, so information like this basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that information kept? In a book? In a file? In a shoebox? Where?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents were placed one on the top of the other as these soldiers came. We knew that it took -- wasn't possible for all of us to remain alive, and those soldiers that would be killed, the documents then would be removed and put on a shelf in Gzim's oda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And speaking of Gzim's oda, I think we can then move to the photograph that's there in front of you, please. Now, first of all, Mr. Karpuzi, what we are looking at here is not the Lapusnik farm compound, I suggest, but we are looking at two compounds divided by a road. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the road is here in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And I'm going to show you the road. I'm not sure we've ever seen this before. If you look at P6 in the locations booklet, please, page 20 and -- 20 first of all and then 21. I guarantee the boy on the bicycle wouldn't have been there in July of 1998, but that's the road, I suggest, between Gzim's compound, the lower half of the single sheet you've got there, and another place opposite. Do you agree? 21 is a different view of the same road. Do you agree with me? That's the road that divides the two compounds.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. Now, looking at the -- that photograph you've got there, please. Could you go back in the book to page 18. Thank you very much. And if you want to look at page 19 as well, this is part of the compound opposite Gzim's, on the other side of the road. First of all, do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one on page 18 I know very well where it is situated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's stick with that for a moment, page 18. Do you agree that is part of the compound opposite Gzim's compound, on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me. Opposite Gzim's house, if you could explain this, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I may be getting it wrong I suppose. Well, I'll tell you what we'll do, we'll look at the single photograph. Let's look at P128, because that we can be sure about. I may be getting that wrong, Mr. Karpuzi, so forgive me. Let's look at P128 together, shall we? The buildings in the top half of that photograph across the road from the compound, they're buildings you have been into, is that right, while you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to that again, please? Can you point to it again, sorry.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There. You stayed there. Right. Show us the oda in which the records you were talking about a minute or two ago were kept, if that oda is on this photograph anywhere. Point to it, if you would.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same or a different oda in which Qerqiz would sing to the soldiers in the evenings?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a different oda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the oda in which Qerqiz sang to the soldiers in this evenings on this photograph or not?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 2 on the photograph. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times, if it's possible for you to say, would you have seen Qerqizi in there and you heard him -- well, no, one question at a time. First of all, how many times would you have seen Qerqizi in there during the war?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember how many times exactly, but I know that's where we sang. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he be the only one singing or would others be singing as well?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Others would be singing as well. There were many who sang. Maybe I am wrong, but I know that many people were singing with ciftelia, our instrument, and I also participated in the singing in the oda.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me, just for the record it's not on the record which building the witness pointed to where he said which oda he stayed in. So if we could put that in, the first oda he marked, which is marked as the oda of Gzim on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. I shall deal with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karpuzi, would you please point again to the -- on the photograph to the oda you stayed in.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that on the photograph you have in front of you have a name written by you against it?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- yes, it has "oda Gzim," Gzim's oda. This is a wall and the sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I hope that's clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I then return to the question I was asking you a moment ago. The other oda that is marked number 2 is the oda in which you saw Qerqiz and heard him sing from time to time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking carefully as you can - and I can show you many other pictures of that compound if you wish - but looking at that compound as carefully as you can, I want you to tell us, please, were there any other parts of that compound you went into at any stage during the war.

utterances.speaker: RUZHDI KARPUZI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it earlier as well that in all the houses that were along the defence line, we did go in and out. For security reasons, as I said earlier when I was asked why, we always thought that in case of shelling, if someone told the enemy that we were staying in those houses, then the enemy would shell exactly those houses. That's why we had to split into smaller group [as interpreted] and in case the enemy attacked the number of the victims would be lesser.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand all of that, the problem is it isn't the answer to the question I asked you. So I'm going to ask you the question once more, please. Would you listen to me carefully. I hope I'm expressing myself clearly; if I'm not it's my fault, not yours. Looking carefully at that compound that contains the oda where Qerqizi would sing, my question, I hope simple: Did you go into any other building or any other part of that compound, other than of course going through the front gate to get to the oda? Apart from that, any other place in that place did you go?
